en.title: Norway vs Finland: 89 % white against 55 %
en.description: Norway vs Finland: 89 % white against 55 %. Snow cover, new snow, resorts and the days ahead in Norway on 18 November.
en.lede: 89 % of the mapped high ground is white in Norway, against 55 % in Finland. The deepest resort in Norway has 55 cm; in Finland it is Kallin with 26 cm.

p: For a trip near the border this decides the direction: the snow is not where the map of borders would suggest, it is where the last storm went.
The white area in Norway stands at about 249,960 km² today, 8,720 km² more than yesterday. Roughly 89 % of the country's mapped mountains and hills are covered.

For comparison, the neighbours on the same day: Sweden: 83 % white, deepest Björkliden with 140 cm, up to 15 cm in the week ahead; Finland: 55 % white, deepest Kallin with 26 cm, up to 13 cm in the week ahead.
At the top of the list, Riksgränsen reports 168 cm.
Then come Sulitjelma Fjellandsby (126 cm), Tromsø Alpinpark (91 cm), Galdhøpiggen Sommerskisenter (62 cm) and Steilia (60 cm).
Riksgränsen picked up 1 cm in the last three days and could add 3 cm by Saturday 21 November.
Sulitjelma Fjellandsby picked up 6 cm in the last three days and could add 2 cm by Saturday 21 November.
142 of the 155 resorts we follow in Norway have snow on their upper slopes.

The rest of the shortlist: Tromsø Alpinpark: 91 cm on top, 9 cm in three days, 12 cm expected; Galdhøpiggen Sommerskisenter: 62 cm on top, 0 cm in three days, 6 cm expected; Steilia: 60 cm on top, 2 cm in three days, 3 cm expected.
Over the next three days up to 29 cm is expected, and up to 38 cm over the week.
The snowiest day looks like Saturday 21 November, with up to 15 cm in the snowiest spots.
The second week adds up to 30 cm where it snows most.
Day by day, the white area in Norway went: 16 November 246,310 km²; 17 November 246,210 km²; 18 November 249,960 km².
Riksgränsen has been the deepest resort every day this week.

sections.h: From the valleys to the summits
p: Average depth of the snowpack by height band: 0-500 m: on average 8 cm (80 % of the ground white); 500-1,000 m: on average 18 cm (96 % of the ground white); 1,000-1,500 m: on average 24 cm (100 % of the ground white); 1,500-2,000 m: on average 29 cm (100 % of the ground white); 2,000-2,500 m: on average 41 cm (100 % of the ground white).

sections.h: How much of the country is white
p: A week ago it was 220,860 km², so the cover has grown by 29,100 km². Snow lies right down to the lowlands and the coast.

sections.h: New snow in the last three days
p: Three-day totals peak at 15 cm, around the Lyngen Alps.
The last 24 hours alone brought up to 7 cm.
At least 5 cm fell over some 76,570 km².

Here is how the deepest resorts compare with their usual 18 November: Riksgränsen: 55 cm at about 708 m, against 59 cm in a normal year; Sulitjelma Fjellandsby: 49 cm at about 465 m, against 52 cm in a normal year; Tromsø Alpinpark: 17 cm at about 222 m, against 37 cm in a normal year; Galdhøpiggen Sommerskisenter: 31 cm at about 2,015 m, against 83 cm in a normal year.
0 of these 4 resorts are above their usual depth for the date.
These depths are for one height on each mountain, below the top, so they read lower than the upper-slope numbers further down.
In past winters the best snow at Riksgränsen usually came early April / mid-April.

sections.h: Planning a day on the snow
p: Above 0 m the ground is almost fully white (80 % covered), so runs up there have a continuous base.
If you can choose the day, go after Saturday 21 November: the fresh snow then has time to settle and the roads to be cleared.

sections.h: What it means on the slopes
p: Fresh snow on top of the base means soft turns on the upper slopes, while the lower runs stay patchy.
With more snow in the forecast, the next days should improve things further.

advice: Snow above the tree line can be wind-packed: watch the ridges.
Read the local avalanche bulletin before going off-piste.
Early-season snow is thin over rocks: ski the groomed runs first.

nb.title: Hvor mye snø er det i Norge? Snødekke og varsel, 18. november 2026
nb.description: Snø i Norge 18. november: snødekke, nysnø, snødybde etter høyde, de neste dagene og de beste skistedene.
nb.lede: I Norge er rundt 249 960 km² snødekt i dag (onsdag 18. november). Det er 8 720 km² mer enn i går.

p: Sammenlignet med 220 860 km² for sju dager siden er det 29 100 km² mer. Snøen ligger helt ned til lavlandet og kysten.
Tredøgnsummene når 15 cm. Mest: Lyngsalpene.
Bare det siste døgnet kom det opptil 7 cm.
Minst 5 cm nysnø dekker rundt 76 570 km².
Nysnø oppå grunnlaget gir myke svinger øverst; lenger ned er det flekkete.

Snødybden avhenger av høyden: 0–500 m: i snitt 8 cm (80 % snødekt); 500–1 000 m: i snitt 18 cm (96 % snødekt); 1 000–1 500 m: i snitt 24 cm (100 % snødekt); 1 500–2 000 m: i snitt 29 cm (100 % snødekt); 2 000–2 500 m: i snitt 41 cm (100 % snødekt).
Varsel for nysnø: opptil 29 cm på tre dager og opptil 38 cm på sju dager.
Den snørikeste dagen: lørdag, 21. november, opptil 15 cm.
Lenger fram, dag 8–14, kan de snørikeste fjellsidene få opptil 30 cm til.
Mest snø i de øvre bakkene: Riksgränsen, 168 cm.
Deretter: Sulitjelma Fjellandsby (126 cm), Tromsø Alpinpark (91 cm), Galdhøpiggen Sommerskisenter (62 cm) og Steilia (60 cm).
Sulitjelma Fjellandsby: 6 cm nysnø på tre dager og opptil 2 cm til innen lørdag, 21. november.

advice: Over tregrensa kan snøen være vindpåvirket: vær varsom på ryggene.
